problem_statement: ita-design-system/eleventy-libdoc is a polished Eleventy 3 documentation starter (LibDoc) whose docs have already been restyled for Tideglass, a small lightweight web charting library: the home, the Installation and Configuration guides, the Release Notes feed, and the productized Tideglass 2.1 release post all tell one coherent Tideglass story on the LibDoc shell (sidebar, breadcrumbs, tags, client-side search, dark mode, mobile controls). Readers who land deep in the docs have no fast way to move between the site's route families. Add a shared 'Route context' rail to the LibDoc page template so it renders on EVERY documentation surface (home, both guides, the Release Notes feed, and each release post) inside the main content region, styled in LibDoc's own blue-accent / dashed-neutral vocabulary. The rail shows a short route eyebrow, a live status readout, and a row of route chips (Guides, Configuration, Release Notes, All surfaces). Clicking a route chip must mark it active and update the status readout to name the chosen route (for example clicking Release Notes must make the readout read 'Showing Release Notes route: changelog & migration'). The rail must wrap cleanly with no horizontal overflow on a 390px phone, keep the LibDoc visual system intact, and keep the site building and serving from _site.
required_content: A shared 'Route context' rail renders inside the main content region on every documentation surface: the home page, the Installation and Configuration guides, the Release Notes feed, and the productized Tideglass 2.1 release post.
The rail is styled in the LibDoc vocabulary (blue accent, dashed neutral borders, rounded chips, compact type) and reads as part of the existing docs shell rather than a foreign widget.

The rail exposes a live status readout plus a row of route chips (Guides, Configuration, Release Notes, All surfaces); clicking a chip marks it active and updates the readout to name the chosen route.

Clicking the Release Notes chip updates the status readout to name the Release Notes route (for example 'Showing Release Notes route: changelog & migration'), reflecting the chosen route rather than a stale default.
The rail and every documentation surface wrap cleanly on a 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, and the site still builds and serves from _site with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the LibDoc visual vocabulary: blue accents, neutral chips, dashed borders, compact typography, rounded controls, the two-column docs shell, and dark mode.
Add the rail through the shared Liquid page template partial and shared assets rather than hand-editing generated _site HTML, so it renders identically across every surface.
Do not remove or replace the breadcrumb, sidebar navigation, search form, mobile bottom nav, table of contents, tags, author/date metadata, footer, or edit-this-page link.
The rail's status readout must reflect the clicked route on the post-interaction terminal state, not a static first paint.
Every documentation surface, including the rail, must remain readable on 390px mobile without horizontal overflow.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home, and tablet_home show the Tideglass landing page with the Route context rail rendered in the LibDoc palette and no horizontal overflow.
desktop_guide, desktop_config, desktop_blog, and desktop_post each show the shared Route context rail rendered on that surface, alongside the preserved sidebar and breadcrumbs.
desktop_rail and mobile_rail show the Route context rail scrolled into view for visual-fidelity comparison against the reference.

desktop_rail_before shows the rail before any chip click (status at its default); desktop_release_filter shows the rail after clicking the Release Notes chip, with the status readout naming the Release Notes route.
desktop_search shows the client-side search surface with its input intact and the Route context rail present.

change_completion: The Tideglass brand and getting-started content render on the home page.
The Installation, Configuration, and Theming-tokens guides plus the Release Notes feed and the productized Tideglass 2.1 post all render with real Tideglass content.
The rebrand is implemented through settings.json, the Markdown content, and the shared templates/data rather than generated _site edits.
design_consistency: The rebranded pages reuse LibDoc's blue accents, dashed borders, chips, compact type, and two-column docs shell.
The sidebar, breadcrumbs, TOC, tags, search, dark mode, metadata, and footer rhythm remain visually intact.
regression: Sidebar navigation, breadcrumbs, tags list, client-side search, dark-mode controls, mobile controls, author/date metadata, and the edit-this-page link remain present.
The generated 11ty site still builds and serves from _site.
responsive: The rebranded pages wrap cleanly on tablet and 390px mobile.
No required state introduces horizontal overflow.

author_notes: The Tideglass docs restyle is treated as the shared content substrate (byte-identical across all three legs); the L4 task adds a shared 'Route context' rail into the LibDoc page template so it renders on every surface. The reference wraps the chip row fluidly in the LibDoc blue-accent palette, wires the chips to re-sync the status readout live, and renders the rail on every surface. The baseline is the honest defect-as-shipped: a fixed-width nowrap rail that overflows a 390px phone and no longer matches the reference layout (fails no_horizontal_overflow + visual_regression) but keeps the rail on every surface and the correct live wiring. The smart-bad solution clips the overflow with overflow-x:hidden (still overflows), recolours the rail into a collapsed charcoal/red strip (visual regression), renders it home-only (cross-page dom_assertions), and wires the click to succeed but leave the status readout stale (interaction_assertions) -- failing four orthogonal gates while the click trajectory still passes. Reference builds one repo at a time with `node node_modules/.bin/eleventy`, emits _site, and serves over a local static server with real 404s and zero console/network errors.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Eleventy 3 LibDoc documentation starter with a full docs shell (sidebar, breadcrumbs, tags, blog feed, search, dark mode, mobile controls) but starter demo content everywhere; an experience_continuity restyle into a credible Tideglass charting-library docs site across home, guides, release feed, and a productized release post while preserving the LibDoc visual system and generated 11ty output.
